precepts.text: It is impossible to renew again to repentance those once enlightened who fall away back into their sin or false religion; that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected and its end is to be burned, the same as 2 Esdras 16:78.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through! It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Hebrews says the same thing.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance”. Those who were once enlightened, who came into this truth, and fall away back into their sin or back into false religion: it is impossible to renew them again to repentance.

“For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.”

That is the field of 2 Esdras 16:78, covered with thorns, left undressed and cast into the fire. The ground that drinks in the word and brings forth fruit receives blessing; the one bound with its sins and bearing thorns ends in the fire.

precepts.text: Meats, drinks and divers washings were carnal ordinances until the time of reformation.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Rome taught that in order to be saved you must be water baptized. Hebrews 6 answers it: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. The principles of the doctrine of Christ are animal sacrifice. The principle goes to the beginning; that is how we got forgiveness of sin at first. And among the things we must leave, Paul names “the doctrine of baptisms”.

Hebrews 9:10 shows what those washings were: “Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation”. Divers washings are carnal ordinances. They were imposed only until the time of reformation, and then they were to end.

So when Hebrews 6:1 says leave the principles, it means leave the meats, the drinks and the divers washings with the animal sacrifices. We did not get perfection in animal sacrifice, and water baptism belongs with those carnal ordinances.

precepts.text: Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet at the laver.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Where did the washing come from? Exodus 30:19: “For Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat”. The priests washed at the laver. This is where John the Baptist got it from.

Isaiah shows what the washing symbolized: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil”. The water was a symbol of putting away evil.

John the Baptist did not make up water baptism. It came from the priests, and John was in the lineage of the priesthood; he was a Levite. So the doctrine of baptisms that Hebrews 6 says to leave is the priests' washing, one of the old ordinances Christ, the new high priest, brought to an end.

precepts.text: Though thou wash thee with nitre, thine iniquity is marked before me.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Jeremiah shows that the water never took away sin: “For though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me, saith the Lord God”. Wash all you want with nitre and much soap; the iniquity is still marked before God.

That is the proof that the washing was always symbolic. It came from the priests, from Aaron and his sons washing at the laver, and it was a sign of cleansing, not the cleansing itself.

So go back to Hebrews 6:1 and stress the word leaving: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. Leave the animal sacrifice, and leave the doctrine of baptisms with it. Rome's teaching that you must be dumped in the water to be saved is going back to what Paul said to leave.

precepts.text: John baptized with water, but Christ baptizes with the Holy Ghost and fire.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
The doctrine of baptisms Hebrews 6 says to leave includes John the Baptist. John said it himself: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”.

John used water. Christ baptizes with the Holy Ghost and with fire, not using water. Christ never used water, because water baptism was to end. It was always symbolic.

So when Paul says “let us go on unto perfection”, the baptism we go on to is Christ's, with the Holy Ghost and fire. The water was part of the principles we leave behind.

precepts.text: Aaron laid both hands on the scapegoat to put the sins upon it.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Hebrews 6:2 goes on to “laying on of hands”, and Leviticus shows where that came from: “And Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions in all their sins, putting them upon the head of the goat”. That is what we did. The high priest laid his hands on the goat to put the sins of Israel upon it.

So Paul was saying: all that stuff the priests were doing, we have to leave it. Christ is the new high priest. The laying on of hands belongs with the animal sacrifice and the washings, the principles we leave to go on unto perfection.

precepts.text: Judas sent an offering for the sin of the dead, mindful of the resurrection.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Hebrews 6:2 also names “resurrection of the dead”, and 2 Maccabees shows how that was handled under the old ordinances: “And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing therein very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection”. A sin offering sent to Jerusalem for the dead. That is how we thought we got the resurrection, through the sacrifice.

So Paul lists them all to leave: “the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. And this will we do, if God permit”. In Paul's letters they were still doing those things. It finally came to an end, with no ifs, ands or buts, in 70 AD, when Esau destroyed the temple, put the priests in slavery, and many of us fled into Africa. It was finished.

And there is no going back: “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”, “If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame”. Some Israelites said we have got to go back to animal sacrifice and water baptism. If you leave Christ and go back to that stuff, you cannot be renewed. They never believed. Brothers and sisters who leave this truth and go back to white Jesus and water baptism, we can't help them.

precepts.text: An oath for confirmation is to men an end of all strife; God, willing to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath.
precepts.point: Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable. An oath for confirmation is the end of all strife; God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and by two immutable things, that it is impossible for God to lie and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth, we have strong consolation. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

note.label: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution

precepts.why:
When a beast left with a neighbour dies or is hurt or driven away with no man seeing it, “an oath of the Lord be between them both”. In layman’s terms he swears: I did not take the stuff, I did not set you up, I do not know where it is. Paul explains why that ends it: “For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.” The owner accepts the oath and the matter ends there; it is not to be spoken of again.

Paul uses this civil law to show how the Most High is unchangeable: “Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us”. The two immutable things are that it is impossible for God to lie, and that he will not take back what went out of his mouth.

God confirmed his counsel by an oath, and that is the end of all strife for the heirs of promise. The same way, once the oath of this law is applied, the matter is over.

precepts.text: Those once enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, if they shall fall away, it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law, so speaking against it is not only with the mouth. Going back into the world and back into the ways that were left is a man's actions speaking for him.

note.label: Matthew 12: Lord of the Sabbath and the Blasphemy Against the Holy Ghost

precepts.why:
“All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.” Not in this world, nor in the world to come.

The Holy Ghost is bound to the law, so speaking against it is not only with the mouth. Hebrews describes the man who does it: “For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.”

These were enlightened; they tasted the heavenly gift and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost. Then they fell away. Going back into the world and back into the ways that were left is a man's actions speaking for him, and that is speaking against the Holy Ghost he partook of. For such a one it is impossible to be renewed again unto repentance; he crucifies the Son of God afresh, and there is no forgiveness for it. That is the blasphemy that is not forgiven.

“For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost”: if you fall out of this truth and follow the heretics twisting God’s law, it is impossible “to renew them again unto repentance.” You are wasting your breath praying they repent; you will see them go into more and more heresies. “And put him to an open shame”: they went right back to their vomit.

Their works do follow them. This is for all of you that want to get paid: “For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name”: shown toward the word of God. Some of us think the Lord is going to forget, so we want payment from man, a Benjamin in my hand right now. That is not the true payment; the Lord said, I got you, I am going to give you power over the nations.
